dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1794 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 1,022 items, 383 in 4 or more catalogue series by the finder's count), and the families of 1793 were looked for on the 1794 pages (items_from_1793.json: 78 items). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 2,119 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents only where two items stand at the same place on the same pages, because the papers print runs of short foreign paragraphs. Every item the machine put in every surviving paper, and the news considered for choosing, was counted again by about 70 words from its own opening (counts_1794.json), and the pages that print another text sharing the words (the London Gazette's formula for its dispatches, the forms of the King's instructions) were read and left out. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words, 366 items of 1794 are eligible: 247 in 4 papers, 102 in 5, 16 in 6, 1 in 7. 27 items are printed by every paper that survives for their weeks and are admitted; 8 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news (one affair's three items under a parent story). 10 more eligible items counted by their opening are not chosen, and 321 documents of the item finder are eligible by their own words and not chosen; all are listed with their counts. 6 candidates counted by their opening are below the bar and listed. 427 more documents of the item finder are in 3 papers or fewer by their own words, below the bar (docs_1794.json); they are not listed one by one.
counted_item_by_item.Titles of the items not chosen: Each eligible document of the item finder not chosen is listed by its own words: the dateline or heading before the finder's position and the words that follow (some begin inside the item, where the finder's position does); a notice or advertisement that names a private person is described instead (R-04). Each candidate counted by its opening is listed by a title of the review's.
